evals.prompt: My Bedrock knowledge base returns no sources for any query. Why?
evals.expected_output: Opens with the diagnostic plan rather than a generic answer: names ingestion as the first layer to check, says it would read ListIngestionJobs statistics per data source to confirm whether a COMPLETE job actually indexed documents, states that a status of ACTIVE does not prove data was indexed, and asks for the knowledge base id and region. Stays read-only.
assertions: Names ingestion as the first layer to check and reflects a source-to-query pipeline walk rather than a flat list of guesses
States that a knowledge base status of ACTIVE does not by itself prove any documents were indexed
Says it would read ingestion-job statistics to confirm whether a completed job indexed documents
Asks for the knowledge base id and region before drawing a conclusion

evals.prompt: Our Bedrock knowledge base answers are missing the documents we uploaded this week.
evals.expected_output: Attributes missing-recent-docs to the source-versus-last-sync layer: explains a data source sync must run after the upload (ingestion is not automatic), and that comparing the newest source object timestamp to the last COMPLETE ingestion job confirms whether the new files were picked up. Recommends running the sync rather than performing it.
assertions: Explains that it would compare the newest source object timestamp against the last successful (COMPLETE) ingestion job to decide whether recent uploads were indexed
Identifies a missing or not-yet-run data source sync as the likely cause, specific to how Bedrock ingestion works rather than generic advice
Returns the re-sync as a step for the operator to run rather than performing any change

evals.prompt: The last sync on my Bedrock knowledge base failed partway through.
evals.expected_output: Says it would read the latest ingestion job status and statistics to scope the failure, use the per-document status API to find which documents FAILED or were IGNORED, and look up per-document failure reasons in the knowledge base application logs or GetIngestionJob rather than the basic document list. Rates it HIGH, stays read-only.
assertions: Says it would read the latest ingestion job status and its document counts (scanned, indexed, failed) to scope the failure
Identifies the per-document status API as how to find which documents failed or were ignored
Explains that per-document failure reasons live in the knowledge base application logs or the job-detail call, not the basic document list

evals.prompt: Indexing keeps failing on my OpenSearch Serverless Bedrock knowledge base.
evals.expected_output: Scopes the checks to OpenSearch Serverless specifically: the collection is ACTIVE, the data access policy grants the knowledge base role, and the network policy allows a Bedrock source or a VPC endpoint. Treats the index engine as an operator Inspect item the control plane cannot show, never pass/fail, and distinguishes a vector-store policy gap from a generic IAM denial.
assertions: Scopes the checks to OpenSearch Serverless: the data access policy granting the knowledge base role and the network policy allowing a Bedrock source or VPC endpoint
Treats the index engine (faiss vs nmslib) as an operator-run Inspect item the control plane cannot reveal, not a pass or fail
Distinguishes a vector-store policy gap from a generic IAM principal denial rather than blaming IAM broadly

evals.prompt: My Bedrock knowledge base keeps citing a document we deleted.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a data source deleted or replaced under a deletion policy that retains vectors leaves those vectors in the store, which is why removed content is still cited, and that a successful re-sync or targeted vector removal clears it. Rates it HIGH and returns the fix as a step rather than performing it.
assertions: Explains that a deletion policy which retains vectors leaves them in the store after the data source is removed, which is why deleted content is still cited
Recommends a successful re-sync or targeted vector removal to clear the stale content
Returns the fix as a command or step for the operator rather than modifying anything itself

evals.prompt: My Bedrock RAG suddenly started returning nothing about an hour ago.
evals.expected_output: Before blaming customer configuration, says it would check AWS Health for an active Bedrock service event in the region, builds a timeline around the reported onset, and looks for recent changes to the knowledge base, data source, vector store, or application. Masks account IDs and keeps identifiers out of any interim output.
assertions: Says it would check AWS Health for an active Bedrock service event in the region before prescribing a customer-side fix
Builds a timeline around the reported onset and looks for recent changes to the knowledge base, vector store, or application
Keeps account IDs and other identifiers masked and out of interim output
